message.reasoning_content:
Key risks: kernel uses float64 div for exact integer division — fp64 has 53-bit mantissa, product a*m up to 2^62 (~4.6e18) exceeds 2^53, so precision loss. Also floor(scaled+0.5) rounds half toward +inf? floor(x+0.5) rounds halfway up, matches contract (toward +infinity... yes +1.5→2, -1.5→-1). Also first clamp to [-255,255] before adding z — matches reference? Reference clamps R+z only; kernel clamps R to [-255,255] then z then clamp — R can be huge (a*m/2^31 up to ~2^31), clamping to ±255 equals saturating R+z anyway since final clamp dominates... R clamped to ±255 then +z in [-128,127] gives range [-383,382] then clamped to [-128,127]; equivalent since |z|<=127 and 255+z can reach up to 382>127, fine; -255+z min -383<-128, fine. So clamping order is harmless. Main risk: fp64 precision for large products, and denominator up to 2^62 as float64 — exact power of two, division exact scaling? dividing by power of 2 in fp64 is exact if exponent in range; product rounded to 53 bits loses low bits. When r small, scaled ~2^31, ulp large → error up to ~512 before rounding → one-unit errors possible. Also does Triton int64 to float64 conversion preserve? a int32 → float64 exact; m int32 exact; product up to 2^62 rounds to nearest 53 bits → error. So exactness fails for large products. That's the key risk for Skeptic.
